question: When only AdamW weight decay is changed during causal-language-model pretraining, does the resulting base model become easier to adapt by supervised fine-tuning, can the weight-decay value that maximizes post-training performance differ from the value that minimizes pretraining validation loss, and which representational, attention-rank, or train-validation-gap correlates accompany that effect?

key_findings.claim: Within the tested range that still yields a usable base model, stronger pretraining weight decay usually improves final supervised-fine-tuning performance across five model groups, but the evidence supports a bounded recipe rather than a monotone rule for arbitrarily large decay.
key_findings.evidence: The authors vary only pretraining weight decay for Llama-2-style 0.5B, 1B, and 4B models at 20 tokens per parameter (TPP), and OLMo-2 1.5B models at 20 and 140 TPP. Across six chain-of-thought datasets, five language/commonsense datasets, and one safety-alignment setup, values above the conventional 0.1 generally beat 0.1 after fine-tuning. Yet the broad Llama sweeps also show that weight decay 3 can begin to degrade performance and weight decay 10 collapses both pretraining and downstream scores; the paper explicitly conditions its conclusion on models with reasonable pretraining loss.

key_findings.claim: The weight-decay value selected by post-training performance differs systematically from the value selected by base-model validation loss in four of five tested model groups.
key_findings.evidence: At 20 TPP, the lowest validation loss occurs at weight decay 0.5 for Llama-2 0.5B and 1B, 1.0 for Llama-2 4B, and 0.6 for OLMo-2 1.5B; at 140 TPP, OLMo-2 prefers 0.1 by validation loss. By average chain-of-thought performance, the best tested value is instead 1.0 for all four 20-TPP groups and 0.3 for OLMo-2 at 140 TPP. Thus only the 4B group has the same selected value, and its three-point sweep places 1.0 at the search boundary rather than identifying an interior optimum.

key_findings.claim: The clearest loss-versus-adaptability reversal occurs in the 140-TPP OLMo-2 group: the validation-loss winner is not the fine-tuning winner.
key_findings.evidence: Weight decay 0.1 reaches pretraining validation cross-entropy 2.6088, compared with 2.6208 at 0.3 and 2.7064 at 1.0, yet the 0.3 and 1.0 checkpoints perform noticeably better after chain-of-thought fine-tuning and 0.3 is the best tested downstream setting. This is a concrete within-architecture counterexample to ranking checkpoints solely by pretraining loss, although it comes from one pretrained run per weight-decay value and only four decay values.

key_findings.claim: Calling the final task score a direct measure of plasticity is a construct-validity assumption: the endpoint conflates ease of learning with the quality and task alignment of the starting representation.
key_findings.evidence: Plasticity is operationalized as performance after a fixed three-epoch fine-tune, not learning speed, gain relative to the checkpoint's zero-shot score, gradient responsiveness, or performance under matched initial competence. The paper's own linear probes show that higher-decay checkpoints already expose sentiment and topic more linearly before fine-tuning, providing a transfer-quality explanation that is not separable from plasticity under the chosen endpoint. Hyperparameter sweeps reduce the chance of a bad fine-tuning recipe but do not identify which latent construct caused the higher final score.

anchors.section: Appendix C.1, fixed three-epoch SFT protocol

key_findings.claim: The direction of the downstream effect survives sizable learning-rate, fine-tuning-weight-decay, and batch-size grids in one OLMo-2 1.5B/20-TPP setting.
key_findings.evidence: A pretraining grid combines weight decay {0.1, 0.6, 1.0} with learning rate {2e-4, 4e-4, 8e-4}, producing nine checkpoints and 54 task-specific fine-tunes; at each learning rate, higher pretraining decay improves average fine-tuning performance. A separate grid fine-tunes four pretrained checkpoints on MetaMathQA and SimpleScaling across three learning rates, three fine-tuning decay values, and three batch sizes, yielding 216 models. Higher pretraining decay wins both when averaging across the 27 recipes and when choosing each checkpoint's best recipe.

key_findings.claim: Correlation coefficients between pretraining loss and downstream accuracy are too unstable to serve as a scaling law or calibrated predictor.
key_findings.evidence: Each model group contains at most ten points and two high-compute groups contain only three or four. Figure 3 reports correlations whose sign and magnitude differ by model and metric; for example, the OLMo-2 140-TPP coefficients are positive (0.24 to 0.38) because worse loss can accompany better downstream performance, whereas Llama-2 4B's three-point coefficients are about -0.96 to -1.00. Leave-one-out correlations in Figure 10 visibly change magnitude and sometimes sign. The authors flag these correlations as suggestive, not conclusive, so the defensible result is the existence of rank reversals, not an estimated global loss-to-transfer relationship.

key_findings.claim: Stronger pretraining decay is associated with more linearly accessible sentiment and topic information, but the paper does not causally connect this representation property to adaptation.
key_findings.evidence: Linear probes on last-token hidden states from SST and AG News usually achieve higher train and test accuracy at every layer as decay increases, across the reported Llama-2 and OLMo-2 groups. Best-layer average probe accuracy is positively associated with average downstream accuracy. The trend is not perfectly monotone, uses only two simple classification probes, and no intervention changes separability while holding other weight-decay effects fixed; Appendix A explicitly labels the proposed mechanisms correlational.

anchors.section: Appendix A, Mechanistic explanations are correlational

key_findings.claim: Weight decay lowers the pseudo-rank of attention matrix products, especially query-key products, but low rank is a replicated antecedent and only a conjectured mediator of plasticity.
key_findings.evidence: Using the fraction of singular values needed to capture 95% of their sum, OLMo-2 20-TPP query-key products in layers 5 and 15 fall monotonically with decay; at decay 1.0 their pseudo-rank is roughly half that at low decay. Value-projection products remain near full rank at decay 1.0 and are less sensitive. The default 0.1 checkpoints are near full rank, and Llama value-projection rank collapses only beyond 1.0 alongside performance collapse. Kobayashi et al. had already derived and observed the weight-decay-to-nuclear-norm/low-rank effect; this paper's added contribution is the larger setting, matrix-specific sensitivity, and downstream association, not the mechanism itself.

anchors.section: Appendix A, relation to Kobayashi et al.

key_findings.claim: The observed train-validation gap shrinks with decay in OLMo-2 at 20 TPP, but this single-checkpoint-family diagnostic does not establish that reduced overfitting mediates improved fine-tuning.
key_findings.evidence: As weight decay increases from 0.1 to 1.0, both training and validation loss trace U-shaped curves while validation-minus-training loss decreases monotonically from about 0.0157 to 0.0135. The paper interprets this as less pretraining-data overfit. No uncertainty across data samples or training seeds is shown, the analysis covers one model family/regime, and there is no matched intervention or mediation analysis connecting the roughly 0.0022 gap change to downstream scores.

anchors.section: Appendix A, Mechanistic explanations are correlational

key_findings.claim: Higher plasticity can trade off against retention, and the appendix's statement that weight decay does not seem to affect upstream base-model performance is too broad for the displayed OLMo-2 140-TPP result.
key_findings.evidence: The stability analysis defines stability as the change in average HellaSwag, PiQA, Winogrande, ARC-Easy, and ARC-Challenge accuracy after chain-of-thought fine-tuning. More plastic checkpoints often have higher post-fine-tune upstream accuracy but sometimes lose more relative to their own base checkpoint. For base models, OLMo-2 140-TPP upstream accuracy declines from 0.61 at decay 0.1 to 0.60 at 0.3 and 0.56 at 1.0, while the three 20-TPP groups change only about 0.00-0.02. Without seed uncertainty, the null-like conclusion is not established and the five-point 140-TPP decline is a meaningful negative case.

anchors.section: Appendix D, Figures 17-18 and upstream-accuracy table in text

key_findings.claim: The 20-versus-140-TPP comparison cannot isolate training duration because the long run also changes the learning-rate schedule.
key_findings.evidence: OLMo-2 20-TPP models use warmup-cosine, whereas 140-TPP models use warmup-stable-decay. The paper uses their different validation-loss optima to support a duration-dependent decrease in optimal decay and later acknowledges that schedule differences may explain anomalous attention-rank behavior. Because AdamW shrinkage is the integrated product of learning rate and decay, the schedule change also alters effective cumulative decay and is a direct alternative explanation for cross-regime differences.

key_findings.claim: The intervention is controlled at the checkpoint level, but absent independent pretraining seeds and contamination checks limit causal and generalization confidence.
key_findings.evidence: The paper states that weight decay is the only changed pretraining hyperparameter within a model group, which identifies the effect for the realized runs. It does not report replicated pretraining seeds, confidence intervals, or hypothesis tests for the main checkpoint comparisons. FineWeb-Edu and OLMo-Mix-1124 are web mixtures, while fine-tuning/evaluation uses widely circulated MetaMathQA, MATH, GSM8K, MMLU, RACE, HellaSwag, and related benchmarks; no pretraining-overlap or contamination audit is reported. Run noise or differential memorization therefore remains unquantified.

anchors.section: Appendix A limitations and Appendix B data/schedules

method.core_idea: Treat pretraining hyperparameter selection as an end-to-end pretrain-then-adapt problem: create otherwise matched base checkpoints across AdamW weight-decay values, fine-tune each checkpoint on many downstream tasks, and compare the decay preferred by base validation loss with the decay preferred by final task performance.
method.mechanism: Five model groups span Llama-2-style 0.5B/1B/4B models and OLMo-2 1.5B models, 20 or 140 TPP, and 10B-210B pretraining tokens. AdamW decay is swept from zero or near zero through values as high as 10, with group-specific grids. Each usable checkpoint is supervised-fine-tuned for three epochs on six chain-of-thought corpora, five cloze-style language/commonsense tasks, and Alpaca-plus-safety mixtures; generation is evaluated through greedy accuracy, majority@16, pass@16, reward-model selection@16, correct ratio, and average reward. Robustness grids vary pretraining learning rate and fine-tuning learning rate, decay, and batch size. Mechanistic follow-ups train SST/AG-News linear probes, compute 95%-mass pseudo-ranks of query-key and value-projection products, measure validation-minus-training loss, and audit retention of upstream benchmark accuracy.
assumptions: Final accuracy after a fixed supervised-fine-tuning budget is a valid proxy for plasticity rather than only transfer quality or starting representation quality.
Within-group single-run checkpoint differences are dominated by the controlled weight-decay change rather than pretraining seed variance.

The selected task mixture is representative of downstream adaptation goals; conclusions need not extend to preference optimization, reinforcement learning, tool use, multimodal post-training, or continual task sequences.
Reward-model scores from Skywork-Reward-Llama-3.1-8B-v0.2 and the Bianchi et al. harmfulness reward model track solution quality and safety in these small-model generations.
The web pretraining mixtures do not contain enough benchmark or fine-tuning material to make differential memorization the primary explanation; this is not audited.

Raw AdamW lambda values are comparable enough across learning-rate schedules, parameter exclusions, architectures, and training durations despite effective shrinkage depending on the full learning-rate trajectory.
Linear separability, attention pseudo-rank, and the train-validation gap are informative correlates of adaptability even though no mediator is independently manipulated.
The best value in a finite grid is a useful operational optimum, including when the winner lies at the boundary of a sparse three-point sweep.

techniques.role: Separately selects weight decay by base validation cross-entropy and by performance after downstream supervised fine-tuning.
Creates otherwise matched pretrained checkpoints while varying the decoupled shrinkage coefficient over architecture-specific grids.
Tests compute-optimal 20-TPP and overtrained 140-TPP regimes, while exposing an acknowledged schedule confound.
Uses a fixed three-epoch SFT recipe across reasoning, language/commonsense, and safety tasks as the operational plasticity test.
Separates greedy, majority, pass, reward-selected, correct-ratio, and reward-quality effects using sixteen sampled solutions where applicable.
Checks whether the pretraining-decay ordering survives alternate pretraining learning rates and 27 fine-tuning recipes per checkpoint/task.
Measures how linearly accessible sentiment and topic labels are from the last-token representation at each layer.
Measures the fraction of singular values needed to capture 95% of singular-value mass for query-key and value-projection products.
Uses validation loss minus fully-trained-model loss on training data as a narrow overfitting diagnostic.
Compares post-fine-tune task acquisition with changes in five upstream benchmark accuracies.

evaluations.setting: Five pretraining groups (physical PDF pp. 3-5 and 14-16): Llama-2-style 0.5B/10B tokens, 1B/20B, and 4B/80B at 20 TPP; OLMo-2 1.5B/30B at 20 TPP and 1.5B/210B at 140 TPP.
evaluations.metric: Pretraining validation cross-entropy and downstream task performance after three-epoch SFT.
evaluations.result: Moderate decay above 0.1 usually improves the fine-tuned endpoint; the best tested CoT decay is 1.0 for all four 20-TPP groups and 0.3 for OLMo-2 140 TPP.
evaluations.baseline: The conventional AdamW decay 0.1 checkpoint within the same architecture, data, duration, and nominal hyperparameter setup.

evaluations.setting: Base-model selection across the main weight-decay sweeps (pp. 4-5).
evaluations.result: Best tested decay is 0.5 for Llama-2 0.5B and 1B at 20 TPP, 1.0 for Llama-2 4B, 0.6 for OLMo-2 20 TPP, and 0.1 for OLMo-2 140 TPP.
evaluations.baseline: Weight decay 0.1 and all other tested decay values in each group.

evaluations.metric: Pretraining validation cross-entropy versus average downstream chain-of-thought metrics.
evaluations.result: Decay 0.1 has loss 2.6088; 0.3 and 1.0 are worse at 2.6208 and 2.7064 yet both fine-tune better, with 0.3 the downstream winner.

evaluations.setting: Six chain-of-thought fine-tuning corpora (pp. 3-5, 16-19): MetaMathQA, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, MMLUProCoT, RACE, and SimpleScaling.
evaluations.metric: Greedy/pass@1, majority@16, pass@16, reward-model selection@16, correct ratio among solvable questions, and average outcome-reward score.
evaluations.result: The higher-decay usable checkpoints generally improve averaged correctness and response-quality metrics across both model families; the magnitude and monotonicity vary by dataset and extreme decay degrades sharply.
evaluations.baseline: Same-group decay 0.1 checkpoints and lower-decay checkpoints.

evaluations.setting: Five cloze-style language-understanding and commonsense tasks (pp. 17 and 20): HellaSwag, Winogrande, PiQA, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge.
evaluations.metric: Per-task and mean cloze accuracy after task-specific fine-tuning.
evaluations.result: Moderate higher pretraining decay usually improves the post-fine-tune mean, while decay 10 catastrophically lowers the Llama results; individual task curves are not uniformly monotone.

evaluations.setting: Safety alignment (pp. 17, 20-21): 20,000 Alpaca instructions plus 300, 500, 1,000, or 2,000 safety examples; evaluation on 100 I-MaliciousInstructions prompts.
evaluations.metric: Mean harmfulness reward-model score on a 0-4 scale, lower being safer.
evaluations.result: Fine-tuning lowers harmfulness, and higher-decay base checkpoints often reach lower scores, but plots show substantial prompt-level error bars and no inferential comparison across pretraining seeds.
evaluations.baseline: The pretrained checkpoint and fine-tuned variants from lower pretraining-decay values.

evaluations.setting: Pretraining robustness grid on OLMo-2 1.5B/20 TPP (pp. 23-25).
evaluations.metric: Six-task fine-tuning performance for nine checkpoints from 3 decay values times 3 pretraining learning rates.
evaluations.result: Within every learning-rate slice, larger decay produces higher downstream performance, while the checkpoint with lowest pretraining loss is not always the downstream winner.
evaluations.baseline: Decay 0.1 at the same pretraining learning rate.

evaluations.setting: Fine-tuning robustness grid on MetaMathQA and SimpleScaling (pp. 23 and 26-28).
evaluations.metric: Average and maximum downstream performance over 3 learning rates x 3 SFT decay values x 3 batch sizes for each of four pretrained checkpoints; 216 fine-tuned models total.
evaluations.result: Higher pretraining decay improves both the average over recipes and the best recipe selected separately for each checkpoint.
evaluations.baseline: OLMo-2 1.5B/20-TPP checkpoints pretrained at decay 0.1 or 0.3 versus 0.6 or 1.0.

evaluations.metric: Pearson correlation within each model group and each CoT metric, plus leave-one-out correlations.
evaluations.result: Correlations vary sharply across groups and can change sign when one point is removed; the stable conclusion is that loss rankings admit reversals, not a reliable global coefficient.
evaluations.baseline: The common assumption that lower pretraining validation loss monotonically predicts higher downstream performance.

evaluations.setting: Layerwise SST and AG News probes (pp. 7, 29-30).
evaluations.metric: Linear-probe train/test classification accuracy from last-token representations and best-layer average probe accuracy.
evaluations.result: Probe accuracy generally rises with pretraining decay and is positively associated with average fine-tuned accuracy, with some non-monotone layers and no causal mediation test.
evaluations.baseline: Representations from otherwise matched decay-0.1 checkpoints.

evaluations.setting: OLMo-2 and Llama attention products during and after pretraining (pp. 8 and 30-31).
evaluations.metric: 95%-singular-mass pseudo-rank of W_K^T W_Q and W_P W_V in selected layers.
evaluations.result: Higher decay lowers query-key pseudo-rank strongly (about twofold at decay 1.0 in the highlighted OLMo setting), while value-projection products stay much closer to full rank until damaging decay levels.
evaluations.baseline: Near-full-rank decay-0.1 attention products and the fully trained released OLMo checkpoint.

evaluations.metric: Validation cross-entropy minus loss of the fully trained model on training data.
evaluations.result: The gap decreases monotonically from roughly 0.0157 to 0.0135 as decay rises from 0.1 to 1.0, while validation loss is U-shaped with its minimum around 0.6.

evaluations.metric: Average CoT endpoint performance versus change in five upstream benchmark accuracies.
evaluations.result: More plastic checkpoints usually retain higher absolute upstream accuracy after fine-tuning but sometimes suffer a larger drop from their own base score.

evaluations.setting: Base-model upstream audit for four model groups (p. 22).
evaluations.metric: Mean HellaSwag, PiQA, Winogrande, ARC-Easy, and ARC-Challenge accuracy before downstream fine-tuning.
evaluations.result: The three 20-TPP groups move by at most about 0.02 across highlighted decay values, but OLMo-2 140 TPP falls from 0.61 at decay 0.1 to 0.56 at 1.0.

limitations: Author-stated (pp. 13-14): the representation, attention-rank, and overfitting mechanisms are correlations; only the effect of changing decay within the realized controlled runs is presented as causal.

Author-stated (p. 14): scope stops at Llama-2/OLMo-2, 4B parameters, 20 and 140 TPP, supervised fine-tuning, twelve task families, and the reported metrics; larger, more heavily overtrained, multimodal, or RL-post-trained models may differ.
Author-stated (p. 14): the 4B and 140-TPP groups have few pretrained checkpoints because of compute cost.

Reviewer-identified: one pretraining run appears to represent each decay value; no independent pretraining seeds, uncertainty intervals for checkpoint differences, or statistical tests establish that modest gains exceed run-to-run variance.

Reviewer-identified: final score after three SFT epochs conflates plasticity, transfer-ready representation quality, initial task knowledge, optimization speed, and downstream generalization; no matched-starting-score or learning-speed metric separates them.
Reviewer-identified: the 4B downstream winner (decay 1.0) lies at the upper boundary of a {0, 0.1, 1.0} sweep, so an optimum is not identified; other group optima are likewise grid-dependent.
Reviewer-identified: OLMo-2 20 and 140 TPP use cosine and warmup-stable-decay schedules, respectively, confounding training duration with cumulative AdamW shrinkage and schedule dynamics.

Reviewer-identified: raw lambda is not an invariant intervention because AdamW's effective shrinkage depends on learning-rate trajectory, batch, step count, and which parameters are exempt from decay; cross-family lambda comparisons should be interpreted operationally.

Reviewer-identified: no pretraining-data contamination or train/test overlap audit is reported for the widely circulated reasoning and knowledge datasets; differential forgetting or memorization could contribute to downstream differences.

Reviewer-identified: linear probes use only sentiment and four-way news topic, pseudo-rank examines selected products/layers, and the train-validation gap is shown for one OLMo group, so the mechanistic coverage is narrower than the behavioral sweep.
Reviewer-identified: the safety result relies on one reward model and 100 harmful prompts; no human safety evaluation, judge calibration, or direct helpfulness-safety frontier is reported.
Reviewer-identified: the claimed null effect on base-model upstream accuracy lacks uncertainty and has a visible counterexample in OLMo-2 140 TPP (0.61 to 0.56).

Reviewer-identified: wall-clock, energy, and full pretraining compute totals are described only coarsely; selecting larger decay by downstream sweeps adds a substantial model-development cost not included in the objective.
failure_modes: Excessive decay destroys both base loss and adaptability: Llama sweeps at decay 10 collapse, and attention value-projection rank collapses beyond the useful range.
A decay selected for maximum adaptability can sacrifice base-model loss, upstream retention, or both, especially in heavily overtrained regimes.
The preferred lambda can shift with tokens per parameter, learning-rate schedule, batch, architecture, and parameter-exemption rules, so copying 1.0 as a universal replacement for 0.1 is unsupported.

If downstream data are scarce, contaminated, distributionally narrow, or scored by a miscalibrated reward model, endpoint gains can reflect memorization or judge preference rather than general plasticity.
Lower-rank attention may move from useful regularization to capacity collapse; query-key and value-projection products respond at different rates, making a single global decay blunt.
More adaptation can increase catastrophic forgetting: the appendix observes occasional stability-plasticity trade-offs even when absolute post-fine-tune upstream accuracy remains high.

A checkpoint with more linearly separable generic features may win fixed-budget SFT without actually learning faster, causing the proposed plasticity proxy to misclassify transfer quality as learnability.
Single-run hyperparameter rankings can reverse under training noise, and the paper's own leave-one-out correlations demonstrate how fragile small-sample summary statistics are.
reusable_insights: Select at least some pretraining hyperparameters against a small but representative downstream adaptation panel, not validation cross-entropy alone.
Report two Pareto axes—base-model loss and post-training adaptability—instead of collapsing them into one supposedly optimal checkpoint.
Parameterize AdamW regularization by cumulative shrinkage or timescale as well as raw lambda when comparing durations, batches, and schedules.
Use boundary-aware hyperparameter sweeps: if the downstream winner is the largest tested value, expand the grid before calling it optimal.
Separate plasticity into starting competence, adaptation rate, asymptotic endpoint, sample efficiency, and retention; a single final score cannot identify all five.

Mechanistic correlates are most useful as stratification variables for causal ablations: independently alter attention rank, representation separability, or train-validation gap and test whether adaptability follows.
A broad downstream suite can reveal rank reversals that average pretraining loss hides even when the two quantities remain correlated overall.
Include explicit negative controls at damaging decay values; they expose the bounded useful regime and prevent 'more regularization is better' interpretations.
open_questions: Does the weight-decay advantage persist with replicated pretraining seeds at 7B-70B scale and beyond 140 TPP under one matched learning-rate schedule?
What decay or cumulative-shrinkage scaling law jointly predicts base loss, adaptation rate, endpoint task score, and retention across model size and training duration?
Does higher pretraining decay improve preference optimization, reinforcement-learning post-training, tool use, long-context adaptation, or continual pretraining, rather than only three-epoch SFT?
Can a matched-starting-performance experiment distinguish transfer-ready features from genuine capacity to acquire new information?
Which parameter groups should receive stronger decay—query/key, value/output, MLP, embeddings, or normalization—to retain the plasticity benefit without rank collapse?
Do causal interventions on attention pseudo-rank or representation separability reproduce the downstream effect while holding weight norms and base loss fixed?
How much of the effect survives benchmark-decontaminated, newly authored, or private downstream tasks?
Can a cheap probe panel predict the downstream-optimal checkpoint well enough to avoid fine-tuning every pretraining candidate?
How does decay interact with optimizer family, muP parameterization, learning-rate transfer, and schedule shape when expressed through effective update geometry?
What is the full stability-plasticity-helpfulness frontier, including uncertainty, rather than only average upstream accuracy and one safety reward score?

competitive_landscape.title: Same Pre-training Loss, Better Downstream: Implicit Bias Matters for Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest omitted antecedent for the claim that pretraining validation loss is insufficient to rank downstream transfer.
competitive_landscape.difference: Liu et al. already construct language models with the same statistically optimal pretraining loss but different downstream performance by changing duration, size, or optimizer and connect the gap to flatness. The target supplies a much more modern causal-LM scale and isolates AdamW decay with broad SFT, but its loss-is-not-enough conclusion is an extension, not a first demonstration.

competitive_landscape.title: Power Lines: Scaling Laws for Weight Decay and Batch Size in LLM Pre-training
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct weight-decay-scaling predecessor and base-loss objective competitor cited by the target.
competitive_landscape.difference: Power Lines models the AdamW timescale B/(eta lambda D), predicts the validation-loss-optimal lambda from tokens per parameter, and emphasizes batch/duration scaling. The target deliberately changes the objective to post-SFT performance and shows that the Power-Lines-style base-loss optimum can be too small for adaptation.

competitive_landscape.title: Weight decay induces low-rank attention layers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct mechanistic predecessor for the attention-rank result.
competitive_landscape.difference: Kobayashi et al. prove the L2/nuclear-norm connection for factored attention products and empirically show decay lowers query-key and value-projection rank, sometimes damaging language-model performance. The target replicates this at larger modern scale, distinguishes the two products' sensitivity, and correlates the useful rank-reduction regime with later fine-tuning, but does not establish mediation.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving Language Plasticity via Pretraining with Active Forgetting
competitive_landscape.difference: Chen et al. explicitly optimize plasticity by repeatedly resetting embeddings during RoBERTa pretraining and measure faster, low-data adaptation to new languages. The target uses ordinary AdamW decay in causal LMs and a much broader task suite, but measures a fixed endpoint rather than the adaptation speed emphasized by active forgetting.

competitive_landscape.title: One Tokenizer To Rule Them All: Emergent Language Plasticity via Multilingual Tokenizers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct causal-LM pretraining-design competitor for downstream adaptability.
competitive_landscape.difference: Abagyan et al. improve adaptation to new and tokenizer-unseen languages through a universal multilingual tokenizer, reporting up to 20.2% win-rate gains. The target varies optimizer regularization rather than representation granularity and covers reasoning, knowledge, and safety, so the interventions and adaptation domains are complementary.

competitive_landscape.title: Pre-training under infinite compute
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest long-duration weight-decay and downstream-transfer predecessor.
competitive_landscape.difference: Kim et al. find an approximately 30x larger-than-standard optimal decay in multi-epoch, fixed-data training and show a validation-loss-oriented regularized recipe also improves downstream benchmarks and data efficiency. The target focuses on single-epoch 20/140-TPP causal pretraining and demonstrates that the downstream-optimal decay can differ from the validation-loss optimum rather than assuming alignment.

competitive_landscape.title: Nexus: Same Pretraining Loss, Better Downstream Generalization via Common Minima
competitive_landscape.relationship: Post-target direct competitor on same-loss/different-downstream optimization.
competitive_landscape.difference: Nexus explicitly changes the optimizer to align task-specific minima and reports better OOD loss and as much as 15% reasoning accuracy at the same pretraining loss for models through 3B. It strengthens the target's objective-level critique with a different geometric mechanism and an actionable optimizer, while the target isolates a standard hyperparameter and frames the benefit as plasticity.

competitive_landscape.title: Can Scale Save Us From Plasticity Loss in Large Language Models?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Post-target direct measurement competitor for language-model plasticity versus training duration and scale.
competitive_landscape.difference: Hernandez-Garcia et al. measure deterioration on a held-out language-learning probe from 5M to 314M parameters and find that scale delays but does not eliminate plasticity loss, even under stationary multilingual training. Their learning-efficiency construct is closer to plasticity loss over time; the target studies larger models and one decay intervention but uses final broad-task endpoints.

competitive_landscape.title: The Kinetics of Training: A Driven-Nucleation Rate Law for Emergence, Plasticity Loss, and Circuit Control in Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Post-target mechanistic competitor linking continued training, hidden plasticity loss, and attention-circuit intervention.
competitive_landscape.difference: Dong reports that learning a withheld capability is delayed and eventually fails as training continues while validation loss still improves, localizes commitment to attention heads, and restores learnability by reinitializing query-key slices. This supplies a duration-sensitive and more interventionist account of plasticity that complements—and narrows the mechanistic reach of—the target's correlational separability/rank/gap analyses.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Larger-than-default pretraining weight decay improves language-model plasticity across model families, sizes, training regimes, tasks, metrics, and hyperparameter settings; the decay that minimizes pretraining loss can fail to maximize post-training performance; and decay may preserve adaptability by increasing linear separability, lowering attention rank, and reducing pretraining overfit.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Controlled decay sweeps cover five Llama-2/OLMo-2 groups through 4B parameters and 210B tokens, twelve downstream task families, multiple generation metrics, nine-checkpoint pretraining and 216-run fine-tuning robustness grids, plus representation, attention-product, train-validation-gap, and retention diagnostics. The 140-TPP OLMo result gives a clear within-group loss/downstream rank reversal.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest remaining novelty is the specific conjunction: a standard AdamW pretraining-decay sweep in modern causal LMs, evaluated end to end on a broad post-SFT panel and paired with attention-product and representation diagnostics. The component claims are substantially occupied: same pretraining loss can yield different transfer (arXiv:2210.14199), pretraining can be designed for language plasticity (arXiv:2307.01163), decay induces low-rank attention (arXiv:2410.23819), and decay scales with duration/batch (arXiv:2505.13738). The paper therefore extends and unifies these lines rather than originating them. Its behavioral causal claim is credible only for the realized within-group, single-seed checkpoint comparisons; 'plasticity' remains an endpoint proxy, and all proposed mediators are explicitly correlational. Later Nexus and training-kinetics work further narrow the loss-is-not-enough and mechanism claims.
